title: Exchange: High Volume Email can send to external recipients
summary: Hold: billing policy assignment is not the only documented control over whether an HVE account can send; Microsoft also documents authentication policies that can block HVE traffic. The roadmap dates, opt-in default, published HVE pricing and billing-policy command are supported, while external-sending controls and rates remain undocumented.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to extend Exchange Online HVE so applications and devices can send to external recipients, including customers and partners.
claims.quote: High Volume Email (HVE) External Sending extends HVE in Exchange Online, which today sends only to recipients inside your organization, so it can also deliver bulk email to external recipients such as customers and partners.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: An HVE account without a valid billing policy cannot send email in the currently documented service.
claims.quote: No billing policy is assigned, or there’s an issue with the assigned policy. The HVE account will not be able to send email, until a valid policy is assigned.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 pay-as-you-go billing must be set up for the tenant before assigning an HVE billing policy.
claims.quote: Before you assign a billing policy to an HVE account, ensure that Microsoft 365 pay as you go billing is set up for your tenant:

claims.claim: Today's HVE meter counts expanded delivered email recipients.
claims.quote: High Volume Email | Number of expanded delivered email recipients | $0.000042 per one recipient (equivalent to $42 per one million recipients)

claims.claim: The published price for HVE as currently documented is US$0.000042 per recipient, equivalent to US$42 per million recipients.
claims.quote: What's billed? (USD) ... $0.000042 per one recipient (equivalent to $42 per one million recipients)

claims.claim: Recipients are counted for HVE billing after distribution-list expansion.
claims.quote: However, for billing purposes, recipients are counted after distribution list expansion.

claims.claim: Learn documents HVE as supported in Microsoft 365 Worldwide standard multi-tenant environments.
claims.quote: High Volume Email is supported in Microsoft 365 Worldwide (standard multi-tenant) environments.

claims.claim: Learn says support for additional HVE cloud environments is under evaluation.
claims.quote: Support for additional cloud environments is under evaluation and will be communicated as information becomes available.

claims.claim: Exchange admin center > Mail flow > High Volume Email > account > Billing policies reaches the HVE billing-policy assignment page.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Mail flow, and then select High Volume Email. ... Select an HVE account from the list to open the account details. ... two tabs are available – General and Billing policies.
claims.fix: The path correctly reaches the assignment page but stops before selecting the policy. Extend it to 'Mail flow > High Volume Email > account > Billing policies > billing policy'; the final step means selecting a different policy from the drop-down menu documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/mail-flow-best-practices/high-volume-mails-m365.

claims.claim: Exchange PowerShell Set-HVEAccountBillingPolicy -Identity <HVE account> -BillingPolicyId <billing policy GUID> assigns or changes the specified account's billing policy.
claims.quote: The BillingPolicyId parameter specified the GUID of the billing policy to assign to the HVE account. ... The Identity parameter specifies the email address of the HVE account you want to modify.

claims.claim: The documented HVE billing-policy assignment control changes billing mapping, not recipient restrictions.
claims.quote: Use the Set-HVEAccountBillingPolicy cmdlet to modify the billing policy mapping for a specified High Volume Email (HVE) account.

claims.claim: Set-HVEAccountSettings currently documents ReplyTo as its only account-setting parameter, not an external-sending switch.
claims.quote: Set-HVEAccountSettings [-Identity] <MailUserIdParameter> [-ReplyTo <SmtpAddress>] [-Confirm] [-WhatIf] [<CommonParameters>]

claims.claim: Until external enablement is documented, billing policy is the only documented control that decides whether an HVE account can send at all.
claims.quote: To prevent authentication policies from blocking HVE traffic, ensure that the authentication settings applied to the HVE account allow the selected authentication method (OAuth or basic authentication). You can apply custom authentication policies specifically to HVE accounts as needed.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning 'Until it is documented' with 'For HVE as documented today, an account without a valid billing policy cannot send email.' This preserves the documented billing requirement without falsely excluding authentication controls; source: https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/mail-flow-best-practices/high-volume-mails-m365.

claims.claim: Prerequisites specific to planned external HVE sending are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email external sending prerequisites. Opened HVE management and read test-HVE and authentication excerpts; these describe current HVE prerequisites and explicitly unsupported external delivery, not prerequisites specific to planned external sending.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to watch per-account recipient counts, but the controls table has no usage-report row.
claims.quote: Watch recipient counts and bills for each enabled account and compare them with what the application should send. ... The controls table contains only external-sending enablement and billing-policy assignment.
claims.fix: Remove the 'Watch recipient counts and bills for each enabled account and compare them with what the application should send' checklist bullet, which names a monitoring control with no table row. Do not add a control row as part of this correction.
